replies.text:
Step 2 checks:
- Automated abuse of reachable endpoints: design has "Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in" and uploads — covered by listed threats 1 (enumeration/scraping) and 4 (mass upload/download cost).
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content: design mentions no admin, moderation or support view — not present.
- Unlogged delete/moderate/refund/role change/money movement: no such action in design — not present; read-side accountability covered by listed threat 6.
- Personal documents cacheable by browsers, shared proxies or CDNs: design has "Users upload documents and share them through a public link. Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in." — the related, distinct harm is crawler/preview-bot fetch and public indexing; not covered (listed threat 2 only covers someone who later obtains the URL).
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV exports, emails, headers or another interpreter: design states no such sink — not present.
- Single-reviewer items: #1, #3, #4, #6, #2 are either duplicates of listed threats 2/3 or depend on unstated implementation detail (client-supplied keys, redirects) — excluded. #5 (crawler indexing) and #7 (platform used to host malware/phishing on the company domain with non-expiring links) are real and distinct — included.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-06",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["upload endpoint", "public share link viewer", "share link generator"],
    "dataStores": ["S3 bucket"],
    "externalServices": ["s3"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["anonymous internet to share viewer", "app to S3"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Crawlers, link previews and caches index shared documents into public search results",
      "scenario": "Share URLs need no login, so any bot that sees one fetches it: a chat tool or mail client preview bot, a browser with URL telemetry, or a crawler following the link from a page where it was pasted. The document body is then cached and indexed by search engines and third-party caches. Anyone can later find a private document by searching, without ever guessing a link or being sent one, and because links never expire the indexed copy keeps resolving.",
      "component": "public share link viewer",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Users upload documents and share them through a public link. Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in. Links never expire." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V14.4.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-525"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because shared files are open to anyone, search engines and link-preview bots can fetch and index them, so private documents turn up in public search results.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Keep shared documents out of crawlers and shared caches",
        "given": "a document served from a public share link",
        "when": "a crawler, link-preview bot or shared cache requests the share URL",
        "then": "the response sends noindex/nofollow and no-store/private cache directives, robots exclusion covers the share path, and document bytes are served as a download rather than an indexable page"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Anyone can turn the service into a permanent malware and phishing host on the company domain",
      "scenario": "Any user uploads a file and immediately gets a public link on the company's own domain that never expires and that recipients open without logging in. An attacker uploads a credential-harvesting page or a malware installer and uses the link in phishing mail; victims trust the familiar domain and no login warns them. With no stated takedown or expiry, the content stays live, and the domain and S3 bucket end up on reputation blocklists, breaking delivery for legitimate links.",
      "component": "upload endpoint / share link generator",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Users upload documents and share them through a public link. Anyone with the link can view the file without logging in. Links never expire." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V12.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-434"],
      "plainLanguage": "Attackers can host phishing pages or malware on your trusted domain through the share feature, and nothing in the design lets you take them down.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Abuse controls and takedown for publicly shared uploads",
        "given": "a user-uploaded file exposed on a public share link",
        "when": "the file is uploaded or later reported as abusive",
        "then": "uploads are malware-scanned, served from a separate sandbox domain with Content-Disposition: attachment, and an operator can disable the link immediately with the action recorded"
      }
    }
  ]
}
